candidates.attacker_control: No direct attacker-controlled request input drives this path; the exposure is a configuration/privilege-assumption weakness. The credential pair (elide/elide123) is published in the same public source tree and is used automatically, so any party able to reach the backing database service (or any local user on a shared host, as the default target is localhost) can authenticate with well-known credentials. Attacker influence is indirect: it requires the deployed service to run with the default properties.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The code path is only taken when the operator supplies an empty Properties object; the block is explicitly commented as defaults for the 'example service'; the same credentials are documented in example READMEs as a local MySQL setup (elide-example/elide-blog-example-resteasy/README.md lines 7-14) and the default URL targets localhost, which limits remote exploitability; production users are expected to override getDatabaseProperties() (the standalone README shows an explicit override). I therefore treat this as a genuine but low-severity insecure-default weakness rather than a confirmed remotely exploitable vulnerability.
candidates.impact: An operator who deploys elide-standalone with its default settings runs the service against a database with credentials that are public in the source tree; anyone who can reach that database endpoint can read and modify the application's data with the application's DB privileges. The same default block sets hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create, so schema DDL is executed at startup and existing schema/data can be recreated or altered, giving a data-availability/integrity impact even without DB network access.
candidates.prerequisites: A deployment using com.yahoo.elide.standalone.ElideStandalone/ElideStandaloneSettings without overriding getDatabaseProperties() with a non-empty Properties object (the framework's own default path); the MySQL endpoint referenced by the effective JDBC URL must be reachable by the attacker; for the data-loss aspect, the schema must be managed by Hibernate with the default branch active.
candidates.root_cause: ElideStandaloneSettings.getDatabaseProperties() defaults to an empty java.util.Properties (lines 237-239) and passes it to Util.getEntityManagerFactory() (lines 66-67). Util.getEntityManagerFactory() branches on options.isEmpty() (line 29) and in that branch unconditionally injects a public sample configuration: hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create (line 31) and JDBC settings javax.persistence.jdbc.user=elide (line 50) / javax.persistence.jdbc.password=elide123 (line 51) for jdbc:mysql://localhost/elide (line 49). Nothing requires an operator to override the default or rejects the empty-properties path, so the hardcoded credentials are applied by default rather than only in the examples that document them (the same credential pair appears in elide-example/*/src/main/resources/hibernate.cfg.xml lines 9-11).
candidates.title: elide-standalone silently falls back to a hardcoded example database configuration (known credentials, hbm2ddl.auto=create) when the application does not supply DB properties
candidates.trace: 1) ElideResourceConfig constructor calls settings.getElideSettings(injector) (ElideResourceConfig.java lines 66-85). 2) ElideStandaloneSettings.getElideSettings() calls Util.getEntityManagerFactory(getModelPackageName(), getDatabaseProperties()) (lines 66-67); getDatabaseProperties() returns an empty Properties by default (lines 237-239). 3) In Util.getEntityManagerFactory(), options.isEmpty() is true (line 29) so the hardcoded block executes: hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create (line 31) and javax.persistence.jdbc.user/password = elide/elide123 (lines 50-51) for jdbc:mysql://localhost/elide (line 49). 4) These properties are handed to PersistenceUnitInfoImpl/EntityManagerFactoryBuilderImpl (lines 54-59) and the resulting EntityManagerFactory is wrapped in a JpaDataStore (lines 68-70), so the application starts against the fixed, publicly known credential set if the operator supplied nothing.
candidates.unverified: I could not verify runtime behavior (no execution permitted): whether a real deployment leaves getDatabaseProperties() empty, whether the referenced MySQL instance is network-reachable, and whether the DDL-create default actually produces destructive schema changes on a populated database. No exploit was attempted and no runtime confirmation exists; this is a source-evidence-only lead.
candidates.weakness_type: Use of hard-coded credentials / insecure default configuration (CWE-798, CWE-1188); aggravating side effect: automatic schema recreation (hbm2ddl.auto=create)

coverage_summary: Scope reported by get_source_scope: 420 model-visible files, no excluded/oversized/symlinked files (parity between B0 and P1). The P1 relation index reports 350 parsed Java files, 2930 symbols, 5537 edges, 87 facts, 0 parse errors, index_status complete, and explicitly no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution or Spring runtime enforcement (qualification: navigation candidates only). I read source in: elide-annotations (permission annotations, checks, prefab checks), most of elide-core (Elide, ElideSettingsBuilder, RequestScope, EntityDictionary (majority), EntityBinding, EntityPermissions, PersistentResource (majority), ActivePermissionExecutor, PermissionExpressionBuilder, expression classes, filter packages, RSQL/default dialects, Operators/predicates, pagination, sorting, JSON-API models/serialization, state machine, JsonApiPatch, audit/LogMessage, CoerceUtil), elide-datastore (hibernate/hibernate3/hibernate5/jpa/multiplex/noop/search main classes and HQL builders), elide-graphql (QueryRunner, PersistentResourceFetcher, ModelBuilder (partial), Environment, Entity, containers, endpoints), elide-spring config/controllers, elide-standalone config/settings/Util, elide-contrib swagger (DocEndpoint, JsonApiModelResolver partial), plus build/doc files (pom.xml, suppressions.xml, changelog.md, READMEs). Authentication of the framework user is delegated to the host container (SecurityContext/Principal) in all integrations.
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, so I could not confirm intended behavior against tests or reproduce any scenario; no code was executed and no runtime verification was possible.
The generated ANTLR parsers and grammar files for URL and permission-expressions are not in the snapshot, so parser-level acceptance behavior was reasoned from the generated visitor call sites only.

Unread or only partially read areas remain: GraphQLConversionUtils, SwaggerBuilder, portions of EntityDictionary, ModelBuilder, JsonApiModelResolver, MultiplexWriteTransaction, SearchDataTransaction, AbstractJpaTransaction/Hibernate transactions, Noop/Jta store classes, and the test-helper module; a vulnerability could exist there and would not have been seen in full.

The P1 index provides syntax-level navigation only (no data-flow, reachability, or semantic resolution); every indexed hint I used was re-checked against source, and its labels were not treated as findings.

The dependent-library surface (e.g. jackson-databind 2.10.3 plus a suppression entry for older databind CVEs) was not evaluated for reachable gadget chains; no default typing or polymorphic deserialization is enabled in the code I read.
Absence of a finding in the traced authorization paths is not proof of absence; the conclusion is limited to the code actually inspected.

rejected_leads.lead: elide-standalone exposes the Codahale AdminServlet (thread dump /metrics /healthcheck /ping) at /stats/* with no authentication, and enableServiceMonitoring() defaults to true (ElideStandalone.java lines 120-134; ElideStandaloneSettings.java lines 196-198).
rejected_leads.reason: Remote unauthenticated information disclosure/DoS is plausible, but the behavior is explicitly documented as the default in elide-standalone/README.md (lines ~344-366) with an opt-out, and no authentication is intentionally provided by Elide; this is a hardening/documentation concern rather than an undocumented defect.

rejected_leads.lead: JSON-API PATCH accepts the non-standard member attributes.id and PersistentResource.updateAttribute() / EntityDictionary.getType() (special case for "id", lines 689-696) can therefore write the primary key; GraphQL explicitly ignores id attributes (PersistentResourceFetcher.updateAttributes lines 450-467), which indicates ids are meant to be immutable.
rejected_leads.reason: Source trace is clear but the security impact is conditional and speculative: the write is still gated by UpdatePermission and Elide's documented 'no annotation = allow' semantics, and JPA-backed stores typically reject identifier changes at flush, so I could not establish a concrete cross-user impact. Kept as an unconfirmed lead rather than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: elide-graphql QueryRunner only calls requestScope.saveOrCreateObjects() when the raw GraphQL document text starts with 'mutation' (QueryRunner.java line 179), while Environment flushes/saves between root fields (Environment.java lines 59-63).
rejected_leads.reason: Produces inconsistent persistence for operations selected by operationName or documents that start with comments/queries, but permission and commit checks still run, so no privilege escalation could be shown; impact is functional/integrity, not a substantiated vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: FilterPredicate.FilterParameter.escapeMatching() escapes '%' but not the '_' LIKE wildcard (FilterPredicate.java lines 192-195).
rejected_leads.reason: Only affects user-supplied matching filters (their own result set); I found no in-repo FilterExpressionCheck whose value contains '_', so non-parameterized wildcard influence on a developer-defined permission filter could not be substantiated.

rejected_leads.lead: Pagination.pageByPages() computes offset as (pageNumber - 1) * limit without overflow checking (Pagination.java line 293).
rejected_leads.reason: At worst yields a negative/huge offset leading to an error or empty page; no data-disclosure or privilege impact identified.

rejected_leads.lead: Hardcoded local MySQL credentials (elide/elide123) and hbm2ddl.auto=create in example hibernate.cfg.xml files and elide-standalone sample defaults.
rejected_leads.reason: This is the same root cause as the submitted candidate; not split into a separate candidate.

summary: Reviewed the Elide 4.5.14-SNAPSHOT tree (420 files; 350 Java sources; test sources are not present in the snapshot). I traced the end-to-end authorization model (JSON-API and GraphQL entry points, URL/state-machine parsing, PersistentResource read/write paths, ActivePermissionExecutor and PermissionExpressionBuilder, filter pushdown plus in-memory re-checks), the query-construction path (RSQL/default filter dialects, Path/dictionary validation, JPQL via bound named parameters), pagination/sorting parsing, the JSON-Patch extension, the Spring and Standalone integrations, and the datastore implementations. I did not substantiate an authorization bypass, data-layer injection, or memory/deserialization/network sink: all read paths I traced re-run in-memory permission checks (PersistentResource.filter / checkFieldAwarePermissions) after any datastore-side permission filter, write paths invoke Create/Update/Delete/Share checks (including commit-check queueing), attacker-influenced filter/sort field paths are validated through EntityDictionary, and JPQL/Lucene values are bound or escaped. The strongest source-evidenced weakness I could substantiate is the insecure default database configuration shipped by elide-standalone: an empty Properties object silently selects a hardcoded, publicly documented MySQL credential pair and schema-recreating DDL settings. I submit that single lead with low confidence and list the other suspicious items as rejected leads.
